To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Ly‐6 A/ E is a T cell activation molecule, that the Ly‐6 A / E pathway of activation is distinct from other pathways, and that the Ly‐ 6 pathway of activation requires IFN and Ly‐6 antibody as well as exogenously supplied IL2.
IFN‐α/β, Ly‐6 and IL2 act synergistically in the induction of T cell proliferation.
Ly‐6 A and E antigens are induced on T cells by IFN, that Ly‐6 antibody induces IL2 receptors on T cells, and that IL2 drives T cells through the Ly‐5 pathway of activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the Ly‐6 A and Ly‐6 E antigens and their role in the activation of murine T lymphocytes.
a pathway of activation which is distinct from that mediated by the antigen receptor, and which requires IFN and IL2.
the identification of a novel pathway of T cell stimulation, the Ly‐6 A pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ly‐6 A and E are T cell activation molecules which are induced by IFN, and whose expression is required for T cell proliferation.
the Ly‐6 A and E antigens are not involved in the induction of T cell proliferation but rather in its amplification.

IFN is a prerequisite for the Ly‐6‐mediated T cell proliferation in BALB/c, but not in C57BL/ 6 mice, and that Ly‐6 antibody induces IL2 receptors and that IL2 is the ultimate growth factor for T cell activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ly‐6‐dependent pathway is an alternative to the Ly‐2,3‐dependent pathway, and is distinct in its requirements.
IFN induces Ly‐6, Ly‐6 induces IL2 receptor, and the combination of IL2 and IL2 receptor leads to proliferation.
the Ly‐6 A/ E pathway of T cell triggering is a two‐step process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ly‐6 A pathway of T cell stimulation is a novel one.
Ly‐6 A is an important component of the T cell activation process.
IFN, Ly‐6 and IL2 are required for T cell activation by the Ly 6 pathway.
